title: Therapeutic climbing in psychatric settings: Evaluation of potential factors and acute psychological changes in inpatients with different mental and behavioural disorders
summary: The aim of the study is to explore the effective factors of therapeutic climbing from the patients' perspective and to evaluate the acute effects on psychological parameters in the interventions therapeutic climbing, endurance sports and sedentary control group. Therefore, on the one hand, the effective factors of therapeutic climbing from the perspective of patients in inpatient treatment will be researched through semi-structured interviews. Two groups will be distinguished: patients with depression, anxiety or obsessive-compulsive disorder and patients with eating disorders (anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa). On the other hand, the acute effects of the climbing therapy with regard to affective responses, anxiety states and self-efficacy are to be compared with the endurance sport Nordic walking and a sedentary control group. All patients will participate in all three interventions and fill out standardised questionnaires before, during and after the interventions. The data will be statistically analysed and put into a scientific context.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnoses of depression, anxiety or obsessive-compulsive disorder, eating disorder (anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa)
sufficient knowledge of German
participation in all four climbing sessions
willingness to participate in an interview
weight under 120 kilograms
no orthopaedic problems
no medical contraindication to climbing and Nordic Walking
Exclusion criteria:
acute psychosis
acute suicidal risk
acute cardiovascular limitations
